
```{r}
library(ISLR2)
library(broom)

```

Instead of using `summary(lm.fit)$sigma` to get RSE after a regression, we can manually calculate RSE of a regression as follows. I use the formula from this note: [https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/what-is-residual-standard-error/](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/what-is-residual-standard-error/)

The model is similar to the main lecture:
```{r}
Boston = ISLR2::Boston
lm.fit <- lm(medv ~ ., data = Boston)
summary(lm.fit)
```



To calculate RSE manually (more useful in case we want to fit model using training sample then use the model to predict a test sample:
```{r}
# Step 1: Collect key information and make predictions from a model
Prediction = augment(lm.fit)
tidy((lm.fit))
Model = glance(lm.fit)

# Step 2 2. Calculate RSE using the training model's degrees of freedom
rse_train <- sqrt(sum((Prediction$medv - Prediction$.fitted)^2) / (Model$nobs-12-1))

```
